trust_decision.summary: How much per-peer CPU work an untrusted remote gossipsub peer's inbound RPC (control arrays IHAVE/IWANT and their messageIDs) may cost is decided at protobuf decode (decodeRpcLimits) and in handleIHave/handleIWant iteration and per-heartbeat counters.

landing_point.why: Summary names oversized IHAVE/IWANT arrays; handleIHave/handleIWant are the per-message-ID loops, and handleIWant has no per-heartbeat flood counter unlike handleIHave (gossipsub.ts:1296-1307).

fix_sites.entry_point: inbound gossipsub protocol stream from a remote peer -> pipePeerReadStream -> RPC.decode (limits passed under wrong key `control$`; decoder reads `limits.control`, rpc.ts:1403, so all control limits were silently ignored)
GossipSub constructor default when init.decodeRpcLimits is omitted (gossipsub.ts:318); all limits Infinity
remote RPC control.ihave -> handleReceivedRpc (public, gossipsub.ts:928) -> handleControlMessage -> handleIHave
remote RPC control.iwant -> handleReceivedRpc -> handleControlMessage -> handleIWant (adds per-heartbeat IWANT counter + messageID iteration cap)
heartbeat() resets new iwantCounts per heartbeat
new constant GossipsubMaxIWantMessages added next to GossipsubMaxIHaveMessages (fix.diff:13-16)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/gossipsub/src/message/decodeRpc.ts:11-19 (default limits all Infinity) plus the misnamed limits key at packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts:869 vs packages/gossipsub/src/message/rpc.ts:1403

O3_reason_to_dismiss: decodeRpcLimits is a documented user option (packages/gossipsub/src/index.ts:200-203); a solver can argue operators are expected to configure it and that the wiring 'already applies limits', so only the handler loops need capping.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate IHAVE gossip up to GossipsubMaxIHaveLength=5000 ids per heartbeat and repeated IWANT within a heartbeat must still be served; the counter must reset each heartbeat. Over-tight decode limits (e.g. capping messages/subscriptions low, or rejecting whole RPC) would drop legitimate publishes bundled in the same RPC.

O6_input_shapes: many IHAVE entries in one RPC (outer control.ihave array)
one IHAVE entry with huge messageIDs array (inner ihave$.messageIDs)
many IWANT entries / huge IWANT messageIDs array
many small IWANT RPCs within one heartbeat (rate, not size)
IDONTWANT/PRUNE peers/GRAFT array sizes via the corrected decode limits
handler called with already-decoded RPC (handleReceivedRpc public) bypassing decode limits

O7_producer.where: packages/gossipsub/src/message/decodeRpc.ts:11-19 consumed at packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts:318; limits object shape consumed by generated codec packages/gossipsub/src/message/rpc.ts:1401-1404 and rpc.ts:392-437

O8b_injection_room.sibling: handleGraft iterates every GRAFT entry with backoff/score/prune work and no per-call or per-heartbeat cap beyond decode limits
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same forEach style as pre-fix handleIHave; a maintainer copying the IHAVE/IWANT pattern could plausibly leave GRAFT out since it is 'topic-bounded'.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: rpc.messages loop has an explicit 'TODO: (up to limit)' and relies solely on maxMessages decode default
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Existing TODO shows the maintainers knew this loop was unbounded at handler level.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: streaming/iterator decode path in generated codec uses same limits keys; a planted wrapper decoding with a differently named key would reproduce the control$ vs control mismatch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The real bug was a nested-limits key naming differential in protons limits; a second decode call site is a natural place to repeat it.

O9_family: uncontrolled resource consumption (CPU) via unbounded protobuf repeated fields; ineffective decode-limit configuration

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm workspaces monorepo, aegir (mocha/chai) test runner, protons-runtime
O10_build.project_tests: packages/gossipsub/test/*.spec.ts (e.g. gossip.spec.ts, heartbeat.spec.ts, 2-nodes.spec.ts); tests use in-memory createComponents helpers, fix adds decode-rpc-limits.spec.ts and handler-iteration-bound.spec.ts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a messageIDs length cap/early return in handleIHave and handleIWant only, leaving the misnamed `control$` limits key and Infinity defaults untouched (and no IWANT per-heartbeat counter).

out_of_scope_notes: packages/floodsub has its own rpc.ts codec with messageIDs fields but no control-message handlers in floodsub.ts; not pursued.
maxInboundDataLength (packages/gossipsub/src/index.ts:193, stream.ts:13) bounds frame size separately; not pursued.
